status.text: The sponsors' committee leaders introduced a substitute amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on November 7.
status.quote: Leadership of the US Senate Environment and Public Works Committee and Energy and Natural Resources committee introduced a subsitute amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026

status.text: President Trump endorsed the amended bill on Sunday night, according to Energy Connects.
status.quote: President Donald Trump endorsed the amended bill on Sunday night, saying it will lower energy costs for Americans.

status.text: The Senate voted 73-25 on cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, the vehicle for BAAJA; Axios reports 51 Republicans and 21 Democrats plus Sen. King voting yes, and 23 Democrats plus Sen. Sanders voting no.
status.quote: The Senate's bipartisan permitting bill advanced in a lopsided vote on Monday, but key hurdles lie ahead.

status.text: The vote was a procedural step; McGuireWoods says the Senate must still complete the remaining procedural steps, consider the substitute and additional amendments, and take a final vote.
status.quote: With cloture invoked on the motion to proceed, the Senate must complete the remaining procedural steps before formally taking up the bill.

status.text: Sen. Schumer said after the vote that he has outstanding concerns with the bill and will seek to address them through amendments.
status.quote: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) said in a statement afterward that he has "outstanding concerns" with the bill that he'll "fight to address" through amendments.

status.text: Sen. Cortez Masto is against final passage unless changes to the National Historic Preservation Act are made, citing tribal concerns, per Axios.
status.quote: unless changes to the National Historic Preservation Act are jettisoned, citing tribal concerns.

status.text: The Albuquerque Journal reports that, per Jefferies analysts, if the Senate passes the bill the House must either accept it or negotiate changes that clear both chambers by Jan. 3.
status.quote: If the Senate passes the bill, the House must decide whether to accept it or negotiate changes that can clear both chambers by Jan. 3, Jefferies analysts said.

status.text: Trump said at a press conference during the Senate vote that he would not approve wind turbines, and that he was behind the bill 100 percent.
status.quote: "I will not approve wind turbines because wind turbines are a major loser," he said during an impromptu news conference.

status.text: The Reuters report says the bill now heads to the Senate floor where senators can add amendments before a final vote expected in the coming days; Energy Connects instead says the final vote is expected in the coming weeks.
status.quote: The bill now heads to the Senate floor, where senators can add additional amendments, before a final floor vote expected in the coming days.

status.text: Energy Connects reports a final Senate vote is expected in the coming weeks and the measure still faces House hurdles.
status.quote: A final Senate vote is expected in the coming weeks, but the measure still faces hurdles in the House.

status.text: Latitude Media's update says the Senate voted 73-25 to advance the bill, setting up full floor debate in the weeks ahead.
status.quote: Update Nov. 10, 2026: The Senate last night voted 73-25 to advance the bill, setting up a full floor debate in the weeks ahead.

status.text: Axios reports Whitehouse pledged a very healthy amendment process, while the House would still need to act on whatever the Senate produces.
status.quote: and the House would still need to act on whatever emerges.

items.author: Axios reporter (unbylined)
items.title: Senate advances bipartisan permitting bill in key test vote
items.summary: Axios reports the Senate cleared its first procedural hurdle on Monday, 73 to 25, on the bill that would limit NEPA and Clean Water Act review, and that the Democratic co-authors pitched it at a pre-vote press conference.

quote.text: The bipartisan Senate permitting bill cleared its first hurdle Monday with a 73-25 procedural vote.
quote.speaker: Axios reporter (unbylined)

items.author: Axios reporter (unbylined)
items.title: The path ahead for the permitting bill
items.summary: Axios reports on the 73-25 vote, the GOP split of 51-1 with only Sen. Rounds voting no, and Schumer's statement of outstanding concerns, and says the House is the next hurdle.

quote.text: The Senate's bipartisan permitting bill advanced in a lopsided vote on Monday, but key hurdles lie ahead.
quote.speaker: Axios reporter (unbylined)

items.author: Inside Climate News staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Senate Advances Permitting Overhaul But Roadblocks Loom
items.summary: Inside Climate News reports the Monday cloture vote, Democratic senators' plans to amend tribal consultation provisions, and environmental groups' objections to the bill's limits on state and tribal challenges to pipelines and infrastructure.

quote.text: The Senate voted Monday to advance long-sought bipartisan legislation to speed permitting of big energy projects, amid acrimony over whether the bill’s support for clean energy will be overwhelmed by the fossil fuel industry’s expansion plans.
quote.speaker: Inside Climate News (reporter)

items.author: Patrick Lohmann
items.title: US Senate advances New Mexico US Sen. Heinrich’s controversial permit reform bill
items.summary: The States Newsroom report says the Senate voted 73-25 to end debate, that Sen. Luján voted no, and that the Western Environmental Law Center called for the bill to wait until January.

quote.text: The U.S. Senate voted 73-25 to end debate on the bill, which requires 60 "yes" votes.
quote.speaker: Patrick Lohmann, reporter

items.author: Source NM staff (byline not captured)
items.title: New Mexico US Sen. Heinrich urges Senate passage of permitting reform bill amid ongoing opposition
items.summary: Source New Mexico reports Heinrich's call for passage on the day of the cloture vote, and tribal, environmental and New Mexico delegation objections to the new amendments.

quote.text: U.S. Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) on Monday urged his Senate colleagues to pass his bipartisan permitting reform bill, even as tribal coalitions, environmental advocates and members of New Mexico’s congressional delegation dismissed new amendments to the bill as insufficient.
quote.speaker: Source New Mexico (reporter)

items.author: Source NM staff (byline not captured)
items.title: All Pueblo Council of Governors condemns US Senate vote advancing permitting reform bill
items.summary: The All Pueblo Council of Governors, which represents 19 New Mexico Pueblos, reiterated its opposition to the bill on Tuesday after the Monday vote; its chairman said the Pueblos delivered opposition statements to senators before the vote and that the Senate went ahead anyway.

quote.text: Nobody consulted the Pueblos before this bill was written, and the changes made since don’t fix that.
quote.speaker: Joey Sanchez, Council Chairman, All Pueblo Council of Governors

items.author: Latitude Media staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Senate’s bipartisan permitting bill passed a crucial test
items.summary: Latitude Media reports the 73-25 vote, the Edison Electric Institute endorsement, and doubts that the bill can pass the House in the lame duck. Its headline calls the vote a passed test; the update line says the vote advanced the bill.

quote.text: Update Nov. 10, 2026: The Senate last night voted 73-25 to advance the bill, setting up a full floor debate in the weeks ahead.
quote.speaker: Latitude Media (update line)

items.author: Nichola Groom
items.title: Senate advances energy permitting bill opposed by some Democrats, tribes
items.summary: Reuters reports the Senate voted 73-25 to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed, and that Heinrich and Whitehouse said the November 7 changes address tribal consultation, utility and environmental concerns.

quote.text: The vote marked an early test of whether the bill’s Democratic sponsors could keep enough of their party aligned behind a measure opposed by some environmental and tribes but backed by labor unions and energy companies.
quote.speaker: Nichola Groom, Reuters

items.author: Albuquerque Journal staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Heinrich permitting bill clears Senate hurdle
items.summary: The Albuquerque Journal reports the 73-25 cloture vote, that Sen. Luján voted no, and a Jefferies analysis that the House must accept the Senate bill or negotiate changes by Jan. 3.

quote.text: Senators voted 73-25 in favor of Sen. Martin Heinrich’s controversial Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act in a cloture vote
quote.speaker: Albuquerque Journal (reporter)

items.author: Just the News staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Senate advances bipartisan permitting reform bill in return from midterms recess
items.summary: Just the News reports the Senate voted Monday to advance the bill as the chamber returned from recess, and that Sen. Whitehouse said the bill would save Americans about $60 to $80 a month. The article also says the bill 'passed' 73-25, which conflicts with the procedural-vote reporting of other outlets.

quote.text: The Republican-led Senate voted Monday to advance a bipartisan permitting reform bill as the chamber returns from its month-long recess for the November midterm elections.
quote.speaker: Just the News (reporter)

items.author: Energy Connects staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Plan to Overhaul Energy Permitting Regime Clears Senate Hurdle
items.summary: Energy Connects reports that the 73-25 procedural vote lets the Senate begin consideration of the measure, that a final vote is expected in the coming weeks, and that the measure still faces hurdles in the House.

quote.text: A final Senate vote is expected in the coming weeks, but the measure still faces hurdles in the House.
quote.speaker: Energy Connects (reporter)

items.author: Solar Power World staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Senate advances federal energy permitting bill
items.summary: Solar Power World reports the Senate advance and cites SEIA's own analysis of the bill's effect on solar, and Sierra Club's statement supporting transmission and clean energy permitting.

quote.text: SEIA conducted an analysis that claims passing BAAJA could spur 167 GW of new solar energy on the grid between 2028 and 2035, while curbing the country’s CO2 emissions by 20%.
quote.speaker: Solar Power World (reporter), citing SEIA analysis

items.author: Zachary Whalen
items.title: Bill to overhaul energy permitting advances through Senate
items.summary: Planetizen reports the Senate advanced the bill 73-25 and that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act still needs House passage.

quote.text: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 still needs to pass the House of Representatives.
quote.speaker: Zachary Whalen, reporter

items.author: Common Dreams staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Days After Midterm Blowout, 22 Democrats Join GOP to Advance 'Massive Giveaway' to Big Oil
items.summary: Common Dreams reports the vote as 22 Democrats joining Republicans (Axios counts 21 Democrats plus independent Sen. King) and quotes Sen. Merkley on shortened timelines and limits on community challenges.

quote.text: It shortens timelines that make it hard-to-impossible for grassroots and community groups to raise concerns about projects.
quote.speaker: Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.)

items.author: Finger Lakes 1 staff (byline not captured)
items.title: Schumer backs permitting debate, seeks changes to protect water and communities
items.summary: The article reports Sen. Schumer voted to advance debate on the bill while saying he wants changes to protect New York's water and local project review, and that the 73-25 vote does not constitute final passage.

quote.text: Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer voted Monday to advance debate on a bipartisan permitting overhaul while warning that he wants changes to protect New York’s water, land and communities.
quote.speaker: Finger Lakes 1 (reporter)

items.author: Heatmap reporter (byline not captured)
items.title: House Moderates Say Now Is the Time for Permitting Reform
items.summary: Heatmap reports on a Tuesday Heatmap event where Reps. Budzinski, Whitesides and Peters rejected waiting until the next Congress to pass the bill, while Huffman and Merkley had argued for a pause.

quote.text: Key House Democrats batted back against waiting until the next Congress to do a major permitting reform bill.
quote.speaker: Heatmap (reporter)
